subject: Grade 10 Computer Applications Technology
title: PC assembly practical (Grade 10 CAT, 40 marks)
task: Assemble a desktop PC in the virtual lab: install the motherboard, CPU, RAM, GPU, SSD and power supply, in the order a technician would, without damaging anything.

limits.about: Ceilings worked out in code from each attempt's log. A mark above its ceiling is sent back to the Marker, whatever a model says.

bands.text: Every part installed in a technician's order: the motherboard first, then CPU, RAM, GPU and SSD, power last. No part tried out of turn.
Mostly in order. One or two parts were tried before the part they depend on, and the learner corrected it.
Order is often wrong. Several parts were tried before the parts they sit on or connect to.
No sense of order: parts tried at random, the motherboard or power supply out of place.
All six parts installed in the right slots and sockets, and the build was finished.
Build finished, with a few parts first placed in the wrong slot before being corrected.
Build not finished, or many parts placed in the wrong slot.
Only one or two parts installed correctly.
Worked independently with no hints, within the target time of four minutes.
Needed a hint or went somewhat over the target time.
Needed several hints, or took twice the target time.
Relied on hints throughout and did not get far.
